crime: Every evening, a girl climbed into the crook of the courtyard tree and called "Good evening!" down to {WITCH_NAME}, who sat at its foot. {WITCH_NAME} could see through the trunk as if it were clear glass. In the hollow, a pair of starlings fed their chicks; she watched them every evening and told no one.
At dinner in the dining hall, the girl told the whole table that tomorrow she would bring the chicks down for everyone to hold. "{WITCH_NAME} will want to see them up close," she added.
{WITCH_NAME} remembered the swifts in her school wall. She had told her lunch table about them, and they were pulled out on a broom handle and passed from hand to hand until they stopped moving.
At twenty past seven, the girl climbed into the tree. {WITCH_NAME} climbed after her, caught her by the ankle and pulled her off the branch. The girl fell headfirst onto the stones of the path.
Whenever a prisoner went missing, the others came to {WITCH_NAME}. She would look through the walls and name the spot, and whoever was missing was always right where she said.
At twenty to eight, in the lounge, {WITCH_NAME} looked at the courtyard wall and told them the girl was sitting up by the hollow, against the trunk, out of the rain.
At nine, the prisoners went out with their phone lights and found the girl dead at the foot of the tree. She seemed to have slipped from the wet branch while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them.

One of them lifted her. The stones beneath her were dry, while all around they were dark with rain. She had been lying there since before the rain began, and the prisoners realized that {WITCH_NAME} had already seen her dead when she said the girl was sitting in the tree.
fields.epitaph: She never learned that the one hand that ever reached for what she loved was reaching to share it.
fields.epithet: Keeper of the Nest No One Is Shown
execution: In the trial court, a great tree trunk rises, split lengthwise and hanging open on its hinge. She lies bound in a straw nest in the hollow of one half. Slowly the halves swing shut, the solid half pressing her down into the hollow. Through the closing wood she watches the spectators outside, every face clear as glass, as the seam narrows. Then the trunk stands shut, straw caught in the seam, and nothing stirs inside.

magic.name: Clear as Glass
magic.text: She can see through walls, doors and anything solid.
